output.summary: Completed the migration slice for the IPC contract transport, local RPC server, and LocalRuntimeProvider guardrails. Targeted verification passed: core IPC contract tests, local RPC server tests, local runtime provider tests, and TypeScript checks all exited successfully. No blocking findings remain. The main residual risk is that LocalRuntimeProvider intentionally allows executable-level commands such as node, npm, and git with caller-provided arguments, so any downstream RPC exposure must continue to enforce strict capability boundaries and avoid granting this surface to untrusted callers.
decisions: Keep the LocalRuntimeProvider command allowlist executable-name based for this slice, treating argument-level restriction as a separate capability-design concern.
Treat localhost RPC protections as sufficient for this migration slice: loopback binding, bearer token enforcement, strict Origin allowlist, request size limit, and schema validation are in place.
Use the targeted test set plus npm run ts as the verification baseline for this slice.
next_actions: Review any downstream RPC exposure paths to ensure LocalRuntimeProvider capabilities are never reachable by untrusted callers without additional authorization boundaries.
Consider a follow-up design for argument-level policies or task-specific command wrappers if LocalRuntimeProvider needs to be exposed beyond trusted local runtime flows.
Run the broader pre-commit checks before merging or committing if this slice is part of a larger PR.
output.title: DW local web portal migration summary

loop_findings.message: LocalRuntimeProvider's command allowlist is executable-name based and does not constrain arguments, so allowed entries like node, npm, or git can still perform arbitrary workspace code execution if exposed to untrusted callers.
loop_findings.evidence: src/runtime/local_runtime_provider.ts:41-43 allows default commands ["npm", "node", "git"], and runBoundedProcess spawns the selected command with caller-provided args at src/runtime/local_runtime_provider.ts:82-88 and 202-206. This appears intentional for a runtime provider, but downstream RPC exposure should keep strict capability boundaries.

loop_findings.message: Targeted verification passed for the migration slice, including IPC contract transport tests, local RPC server tests, RuntimeProvider guardrail tests, and TypeScript checks.
loop_findings.evidence: Dynamic Workflow verification shows npm test -- src/ipc/contracts/core.test.ts passed 8 tests, npm test -- src/server/local_rpc_server.test.ts passed 7 tests, npm test -- src/runtime/local_runtime_provider.test.ts passed 6 tests, and npm run ts exited 0.

loop_findings.message: Local RPC server has the expected core localhost protections for this slice: loopback bind enforcement, required bearer token, strict allowlisted Origin, request body size cap, and contract input/output validation.
loop_findings.evidence: src/server/local_rpc_server.ts:43-60 validates token/origins/loopback host, src/server/local_rpc_server.ts:141-154 checks Origin then token before dispatch, src/server/local_rpc_server.ts:165-186 validates input/output schemas, and src/server/local_rpc_server.ts:257-291 enforces JSON parsing and max body bytes.
